setlist.title: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (3 reviews): Scarlet into Eyes is singled out as a standout, alongside Tom Thumb and The Wheel; Scarlet into Eyes transition called flawless [31][33][41]
- **Bertha** (1 review): First set Bertha, Brown-Eyed Women, Cold Rain and Music singled out as great [33]
- **Little Red Rooster** (1 review): Named among the highlights of the show [30]
- **My Brother Esau** (1 review): Reviewer wonders why Bob stopped playing My Brother Esau, calling it one of his better songs [38]
- **Just Like Tom Thumb's Blues** (1 review): The Tom Thumb, Cold Rain and Music Never Stopped sequence is called among the finest moments of 1985 [37]
- **The Wheel** (1 review): The Wheel into Truckin' is picked out as a highlight [30]
- **The Other One** (1 review): The Other One is described as screaming [37]

## Setlist highlights

- **Bill Graham intro - tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [42]
- **Bill Graham announcement**: back after 955 archived shows (5004 days); rare: 3 archived performances [42]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-04-27.151970.Mouth.AKG.Rogers.Noel.fixed.151703.t-flac2496** (recommended): source not stated; 24 songs; 170 min [1]. Said about its sound: Described as a huge recording from the mouth; Dan Healy's mix had a hiccup that night [1]
- **gd1985-04-27.151703.Mouth.AKG.Master.Cassette.Rogers.Noel.t-flac2496**: source not stated; 24 songs; 170 min [3]
- **gd1985-04-27.mtx.haugh.78504.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 154 min; rated 5/5 by 4 [4]
- **gd1985-04-27.172444.nak300.terry.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 153 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [6]
- **gd85-04-27.sbd.jerugim.359.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 147 min; rated 4.45/5 by 31 [11]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sounds superb, though Jerry's voice is frog-like; second-set transitions are called sloppy but inspired; Soundboard is crisp and punchy, with Garcia's playing described as flawless; Soundboard is described as pristine [30][31][32]
- **gd85-04-27.sbd.unknown.17265.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 147 min; rated 4.25/5 by 8 [12]. Said about its sound: Soundboard is described as great sounding and well played [38]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: taper [1]
- Second set praised for unexpected turns into different songs and for transitions that are not sloppy [32]
- Jerry says of Phil that the band is hanging on to him a little while [33]
- It was a bright, sunny day at Frost [37]
- Tapers were busted during Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad but kept recording [1]
- Taper bust occurred during Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad, yet the tapers kept rolling [3]
- Calls 1985 full of unpredictable, great shows despite Jerry's poor health and singing; says 1986 was a down year [39]
- Reviewer says 1985 was known as a down year, but this show is solid throughout [41]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-04-27.151970.Mouth.AKG.Rogers.Noel.fixed.151703.t-flac2496**: taped by Recording by Craig Rogers; transferred by Transfer by Craig Rogers Edited & Mastered (Adobe Audition) by Joe Noel January 20, 2021; source: Source: AKG CE1s (ORTF) > Uher CR240 > Master Cassettes Location: Mouth, ten heads back from stage lip, Phil's side, Set I & Set II through GDTRFB; OTS, MSWS… [1]. Also: Recorded from the mouth of the stage by Craig Rogers with AKG mics; pitch corrected, with tape pauses cross faded [1]
- **gd1985-04-27.151703.Mouth.AKG.Master.Cassette.Rogers.Noel.t-flac2496**: taped by Craig Rogers; transferred by Transfer by Craig Rogers Edited & Mastered (Adobe Audition) by Joe Noel January 20, 2021; source: Source: AKG CE1s (ORTF) > Uher CR240 > Master Cassettes [3]. Also: Master cassette from Craig Rogers, taped with AKG mics near the stage mouth; pitch corrected, pauses cross faded [3]
- **gd1985-04-27.mtx.haugh.78504.flac16**: taped by See info file; transferred by Dan Haugh; source: SBD + AUD Matrix 3 Source Mix [4]. Also: Soundboard transferred and edited by Charlie Miller via Sony R500 DAT; audience mics on a T bar, knee high toward the stacks [4]
- **gd1985-04-27.172444.nak300.terry.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Mark Terry; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Mark Terry's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 300 mics > Sony WM-D6C (Maxell XLII-S90) [6]. Also: Bob Wagner's Nakamichi 700 source supplies patches in the Eyes of the World transition and the Truckin' into The Other One transition [6]
- **gd85-04-27.sbd.jerugim.359.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBDMC> DAT> CDR [11]
- **gd85-04-27.sbd.unknown.17265.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > MC > DAT > CDR > EAC > mkwACT [12]

claims.text: Named among the highlights of the show
Soundboard sounds superb, though Jerry's voice is frog-like; second-set transitions are called sloppy but inspired
The Wheel into Truckin' is picked out as a highlight
Soundboard is crisp and punchy, with Garcia's playing described as flawless
Scarlet into Eyes is singled out as a standout, alongside Tom Thumb and The Wheel
Soundboard is described as pristine
Second set praised for unexpected turns into different songs and for transitions that are not sloppy
Scarlet into Eyes transition called flawless
First set Bertha, Brown-Eyed Women, Cold Rain and Music singled out as great
Jerry says of Phil that the band is hanging on to him a little while
The Tom Thumb, Cold Rain and Music Never Stopped sequence is called among the finest moments of 1985
It was a bright, sunny day at Frost
The Other One is described as screaming
Soundboard is described as great sounding and well played
Reviewer wonders why Bob stopped playing My Brother Esau, calling it one of his better songs
Calls 1985 full of unpredictable, great shows despite Jerry's poor health and singing; says 1986 was a down year
Scarlet into Eyes into Goin' Down the Road is called a rare sequence
Reviewer says 1985 was known as a down year, but this show is solid throughout
Recorded from the mouth of the stage by Craig Rogers with AKG mics; pitch corrected, with tape pauses cross faded
Tapers were busted during Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad but kept recording
Described as a huge recording from the mouth; Dan Healy's mix had a hiccup that night
Master cassette from Craig Rogers, taped with AKG mics near the stage mouth; pitch corrected, pauses cross faded
Taper bust occurred during Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad, yet the tapers kept rolling
Soundboard transferred and edited by Charlie Miller via Sony R500 DAT; audience mics on a T bar, knee high toward the stacks
Master cassette source from Mark Terry, transferred by Charlie Miller, with Nakamichi 300 gear named
Bob Wagner's Nakamichi 700 source supplies patches in the Eyes of the World transition and the Truckin' into The Other One transition
